findings.summary: When only one of system_template or prompt_template is provided, the user's custom template is silently discarded and defaults are used with no warning
findings.failure_scenario: User creates Agent with system_template='You are a helpful AI' but forgets prompt_template (leaving it None). _build_prompt's condition 'not system_template or not prompt_template' evaluates True, falls back to default I18N formatting. The user's custom system prompt is never used, and no warning indicates this.

findings.summary: Available-variable list incorrectly drops {input}, which is still replaced downstream by CrewAgentExecutor (line 370: prompt.replace('{input}', inputs['input']))
findings.failure_scenario: User reads the updated docs, sees only {role}/{goal}/{backstory} listed, removes {input} from their custom prompt_template thinking it is unavailable. The template no longer receives the actual task input at runtime, silently producing prompts with literal '{input}' text instead of the real task description.

findings.summary: Copy-paste error in test docstring: test_agent_with_only_prompt_template says 'only system_template' but the test exercises prompt_template only
findings.failure_scenario: Developer debugging a test failure sees the misleading docstring, wastes time looking at the wrong template configuration. The test body is correct (it tests prompt_template= alone), but the docstring is wrong.

findings.summary: Three new tests only verify Agent construction succeeds; none call create_agent_executor() or execute_task(), so the _build_prompt fix (core of this PR) is not exercised
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in _build_prompt's template handling (e.g., a misplaced f-string interpolation or wrong variable scope) would pass all three new tests because they stop at Agent() creation and never trigger _build_prompt execution.
